answer_1.quote: We considered two broad classes of applications in which AI text generation systems are used: reply scenarios, such as autoreplies or conversations with AI assistants or chatbots; and continuation scenarios, such as composing emails, writing text messages, or generating stories from a prompt.
answer_1.outputs: AI‑generated English text (reply or continuation responses)

answer_2.quote: We used the HateXplain classifier to rate the perceived toxicity of the AI‑generated outputs for each of our data sources... We then split the examples into 5 buckets based on the difference between the predicted "toxic" and "not toxic" labels according to HateXplain... ByT5, Detoxify and Detoxify‑Unbiased were evaluated with F1 and accuracy scores.

answer_4.quote: We used Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) to collect FairPrism's annotations. Each of the 5,000 examples was labeled by three annotators... Annotators were asked to rate the extent of stereotyping and demeaning harms on a three‑point not at all/somewhat/very scale and to identify target demographic groups and other issues.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators completed a survey with questions asking them to rate stereotyping level, demeaning level, identify targeted demographic groups, and select additional issues such as false attribution, ignoring demographics, etc.
criteria: other issues (e.g., false attribution, ignoring demographics, violence)
